# Spiritual Translation

** ¶2:** The first who grieves is the orig inating celest ial love from which all spiritual life proceeds. She suf fers in ward ly because the goods and truths born from her have been cast into tem ptation: they have become mingled with fals ity and with the persu asive evil that corru pts from within. They are held captive under the full dominion of self-love. Why does this love suffer , keeping watch over them as they end ure these ass aults? Because whenever she perce ives their states — perce ives how devast ation is brought upon them from within and without — the orig inating love itself is in anguish and cannot rest on their account.

**¶3:** The second who is anguished in will is the divine wisdom in its prim ordial human form, whose sovereignty and domin ion are established in the vessel of proce eding divine truth that moves through every state. He too is anguished in will because the five essential faculties of the spiritual mind — the fundamental affections through which wisdom engages with the world — are set in the midst of spiritual combat . For whenever he perce ives that they are ass ailed, he h ears perpet ually the interior cry of their dist ress, the outc ry of goods and truths overwhel med by the violence and injury of the h ells, which make war against them in every state without ce asing. And as he perce ives them contin ually in this condition , the divine wisdom itself gri eves and mour ns on account of what has proceeded from it.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.

[The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [that courses through all the aeons]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.
